existing.description: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships support researchers holding a PhD who wish to carry out their research activities abroad, acquire new skills and develop their careers. There are two types: European Postdoctoral Fellowships, lasting 12 to 24 months in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and open to any nationality; and Global Postdoctoral Fellowships, lasting an outgoing phase of 12 to 24 months in a non-associated Third Country followed by a mandatory 12-month return phase, open only to nationals or long-term residents of EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries. The researcher is recruited by a host organisation, which submits the proposal through the EU Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal, and receives a living allowance, a mobility allowance and, where applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. The 2026 call closed on 9 September 2026 and the 2027 call opens on 7 April 2027 with a deadline of 8 September 2027, both indicative.
eligibility: PhD degree held at the time of the application deadline, or doctoral thesis successfully defended even if the degree is not yet formally awarded
Maximum of eight years of research experience counted from the award of the PhD, with years outside research, career breaks and, for reintegration cases, research in third countries excluded

Mobility rule: not more than 12 months of residence or main activity in the beneficiary country for a European Postdoctoral Fellowship, or in the outgoing-phase host organisation's country for a Global Postdoctoral Fellowship, during the 36 months immediately before the call deadline
Global Postdoctoral Fellowships: nationals or long-term residents of EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries

For Euratom Research and Training Programme research areas: national or long-term resident of an EU Member State or Euratom Associated Country, and the beneficiary organisation must also be established in an EU Member State or Euratom Associated Country
existing.eligibility_summary: Excellent researchers of any nationality holding a PhD; mobility rule (must not have resided/worked in recruiting country >12 months in past 36 months); open to those reintegrating to Europe or displaced by conflict.
benefits: Salary, mobility allowance, research costs, training and networking support (typical total €100,000+ over fellowship duration)
coverage: Salary, mobility allowance, research costs, training and networking support (typical total €100,000+ over fellowship duration)
requirements: online manual on how to submit an application
application_method: Joint application by researcher and host institution
existing.best_fit: Postdoctoral researchers seeking fully funded research fellowships across EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries.
existing.notes: Standard duration 12–24 months; two tracks: European Postdoctoral Fellowship and Global Postdoctoral Fellowship.
existing.duration: European Postdoctoral Fellowships: 12 to 24 months. Global Postdoctoral Fellowships: an outgoing phase of 12 to 24 months in a non-associated Third Country plus a mandatory 12-month return phase in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
existing.application_period: Annual call. The 2026 call ran from 9 April 2026 and closed on 9 September 2026 at 17:00 CEST. The 2027 call opens 7 April 2027 and closes 8 September 2027, both marked to be confirmed.
existing.program_type: EU research grant / research fellowship under Horizon Europe, administered by the European Research Executive Agency

existing.description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is open to short-cycle, Bachelor's and Master's students and to doctoral candidates registered at a participating higher education institution and enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree. There is no central application form: students apply through the international or Erasmus+ office of their own institution, which selects applicants fairly and transparently. The grant contributes to travel and daily living costs with amounts varying by destination and demand, and Erasmus+ students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library fees at the receiving institution. Mobilities run from 2 to 12 months for long-term study, or 5 to 30 days for short-term blended mobility, with up to 12 months in total per study cycle.
eligibility: Student at short-cycle, Bachelor's or Master's level, or a doctoral candidate
Registered at a higher education institution that participates in the Erasmus+ programme and holds an Erasmus Charter for Higher Education
Enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification
The study period abroad must be relevant for degree-related learning and personal development needs
The study period abroad must be part of the study programme the student is following
The sending and receiving institutions must have an inter-institutional agreement, and both must hold the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education where applicable
existing.eligibility_summary: Students currently enrolled in a higher education institution that participates in Erasmus+; studying in a recognized degree program; exchange must be relevant to degree-related learning.
benefits: Tuition fees waived at host institution
Monthly living grant (amount varies by country)
Additional support for students with disabilities
coverage: Tuition fees waived at host institution
Monthly living grant (amount varies by country)
Additional support for students with disabilities
existing.english_requirement: No Erasmus+ English test requirement is published. Language support is provided through Erasmus+ Online Language Support (OLS), and the language of study is set by the receiving institution.
application_method: Through sending home university's international/Erasmus+ office
existing.best_fit: University-enrolled students seeking short-term study abroad funding within the Erasmus+ network.
existing.notes: 2–12 months abroad (or 5–30 days for short-term blended mobility); maximum 12 months total per study cycle; distinct from Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (full degree program).
existing.duration: Long-term mobility: minimum 2 months to maximum 12 months abroad, including blended mobilities with a virtual component. Short-term mobility: 5 to 30 days abroad, which must be blended mobilities; only doctoral candidates can do a short-term mobility without a virtual component. Maximum total duration is 12 months within one study cycle, with more than one exchange possible within that limit. For one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture, up to 24 months.
existing.application_period: Year-round through the sending institution, which publishes its own Erasmus+ selection deadlines for each academic year.
existing.deadline_display: Varies by university (typically 1–3 months before departure)
existing.program_type: EU exchange and mobility programme (Erasmus+ Key Action 1), funded by the European Commission
